# ethereum-optimism/specs Daily Update (Aug 27, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today's activity focused on refining specifications, addressing critical issues in `kona-node` related to sequencer stability and network performance, and conducting a thorough audit of documentation references for starter examples. A new pull request was opened to remove the Alt-DA specification.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

- **Specification Refinement**: A new pull request was opened to remove the Alt-DA specification, indicating a potential shift or simplification in data availability strategies. [#935](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/935)

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
- **specs: remove Alt-DA specification** ([#935](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/935)): This pull request proposes the removal of the Alt-DA specification.

## CLOSED ISSUES

- **Rollup Configuration Leniency**: The issue regarding `kona-genesis` silently accepting unknown keys in `RollupConfig` was closed as "not planned." The leniency is deliberate to support loading older configurations with retired keys, and the superchain-registry config tests already cover fields not yet modeled by Kona. [#22682](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/22682)
- **Supernode Interoperability Wedge**: An issue detailing a cross-safe wedge in the `op-supernode` after an invalid-message replacement was closed. Analysis revealed it was a single occurrence in 7.5 weeks, with the root cause traced to chain 901 rejecting batches due to a parent-hash mismatch, pointing to an oscillation issue rather than a distinct cross-safety bug. [#22325](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/22325)

## NEW ISSUES

- **SuperchainERC20 Compatibility Checking Gap**: A new issue highlights the lack of a supported method for developers to verify if a token address is SuperchainERC20 compatible. This capability is deemed crucial, especially with the potential revival of `SuperchainTokenBridge` and `SuperchainERC20` contracts. [#1020](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/1020)

## ACTIVE ISSUES

- **`kona-node` NetworkActor Stalling**: Discussion on [#22646](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/22646) indicates that the `NetworkActor` in `kona-node` can stall the p2p swarm during remote-signer HTTP calls. A contributor has offered to pick up the issue, proposing to investigate overflow policy and the possibility of landing a deadline change separately from other restructuring. They also plan to confirm the stalling behavior by running `kona-node` against a signer with injected latency.

- **`kona-node` Sequencer Stuck in `forkchoiceUpdated` Loop**: Issue [#22681](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/22681) describes a scenario where a `kona-node` sequencer can become permanently wedged in a `engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV3` loop. A related fix in [#22686](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/22686) addresses the reported wedge, but three pre-existing gaps remain: `SealTask` errors not triggering a reset, `QueuedSequencerEngineClient`'s `recv().await` calls lacking timeouts, and the sequencer's next parent coming from a lagging watch channel. The discussion notes that with the backoff from the fix, the failure mode changes from a CPU-pinned node to retries at ~1.3s intervals.

- **Starter Examples Documentation Audit**: Issue [#1014](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/1014) reports that a comprehensive audit of documentation references for starter examples is complete. The audit found no live documentation links to any of the six starter repos or four archive-sweep repos, meaning archiving these repos will not break published documentation. The blast radius for cross-references is self-contained, with only three external links needing attention in other READMEs. An incidental finding noted that live docs still link to the archived `github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs` repo.

- **Starter Examples Consolidation**: Discussion on [#1015](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/1015) proposes consolidating five `superchain-starter*` repositories into a single `superchain-starter` repo, while keeping `superchainerc20-starter` independent due to its distinct nature and popularity. The recommendation is to use a plain copy with pointers to the original repos for history preservation. The inbound link fix-up list is small, with no live documentation links affected. The execution is currently blocked by write access permissions.

- **Archive Sweep for Abandoned Repos**: Issue [#1017](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/1017) details the completion of an inbound-link check for four abandoned repositories. No live documentation links any of these repos. The remaining fix-up work involves two README edits. The issue also clarifies the purpose of `superchainerc20-compatibility`, noting it was an unfinished project for checking token compliance, with roughly half of its checks now obsolete due to changes in the OP Stack. The archiving process is blocked by organizational admin permissions.
